title: requirements.txt omits Flask — documented setup fails in a clean env
evidence: requirements.txt lists only `pytest==7.4.3`; app.py:5 `from flask import Flask, ...`. README.md:22-30 instructs `pip install -r requirements.txt` then `python app.py`, which raises ModuleNotFoundError: flask on a fresh install. (Scored run passed only because flask was already present: test_coverage=0.94.)
suggestion: Add `Flask>=3.0` (and pin it) to requirements.txt so the documented run instructions work reproducibly.

title: Tests do not isolate the database — they run against the real books.db
evidence: test_app.py:18 sets `app.config['DATABASE']=db_path`, but app.py:8 defines a module-level `DATABASE='books.db'` that get_db()/init_db() (app.py:15,30) use directly and never read from app.config. The temp db created at test_app.py:14 is unlinked unused; tests read/write books.db in cwd and the autouse fixture (test_app.py:32-42) DELETEs all rows.
suggestion: Make get_db()/init_db() read the DB path from app.config['DATABASE'] (fallback to the constant) so the fixture's temp DB is actually used and tests don't mutate a real books.db.

title: author filter is substring match, not exact
evidence: app.py:117 uses `WHERE author LIKE '%'||?||'%'` (f-string `%{author}%`), so ?author=Author+A matches 'Author AB' too; the test relies on substring semantics (test_app.py:145-146).
suggestion: Fine as an enhancement; document that ?author= is a substring/contains match if exactness is expected.
